##: QQ Music (QQ音乐) PC client from y.qq.com.

The download page https://y.qq.com/n/ryqq_v2/download_detail/pc is a JS shell; the release feed is https://y.qq.com/download/download.js, a JSONP payload whose first entry ("Windows PC") carries the display version, the setup file name and the download signature.

The installer is gated behind a per-file signature: c.y.qq.com/cgi-bin/file_redirect.fcg answers 403 to an unsigned request and 302 to dldir.y.qq.com only when sign matches the file name, and the sign changes with every release. checkver therefore captures (?<sign>) together with (?<setup>) and autoupdate rebuilds both halves of the URL.

The payload is a Tencent TinyInstaller wrapper: 7-Zip lists only the PE stub, while the 332 MB client sits in a proprietary container (the installer references it as ProgramFiles.7z) that does not expose a standard archive header. The manifest therefore uses the vendor's documented silent switches instead of extracting.

installdir is the parent of the client folder. Passing $dir makes the installer create $dir\QQMusic and record that path under HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Tencent\QQMusic, so bin and shortcuts point one level down rather than moving the tree and breaking the installer's own bookkeeping.

The feed's Fversion value is prefixed with a localized label, so the regex steps over everything before the first dotted number instead of matching the label text; the display version (22.8.2) differs from the PE file version (22.82) and from the setup suffix (2282).
desktopshortcut/songrecognitionshortcut/autostart are disabled so that Scoop's Start Menu entry is the only shortcut created.
The vendor's own uninstaller is run silently on 'scoop uninstall' (it is the only thing that clears HKLM and the QQ-specific file associations); the Test-Path guard covers a half-finished install.

The #/dl.exe fragment only renames the cached download: without it Scoop would save the response as file_redirect.fcg and then try to execute that name. The file is a plain PE, so Invoke-Extraction leaves it alone and Invoke-Installer runs it.
No checksum is published, so autoupdate.hash is omitted and Excavator downloads the full 113 MB setup to refresh the hash.
description: QQ Music (QQ音乐) desktop music streaming client
notes: Installed with the vendor's silent switches into $dir\QQMusic; the installer also registers an uninstall entry, HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Tencent\QQMusic and the QQ-specific audio associations (qmc/mflac/mgg/qrc). 'scoop uninstall' runs the vendor uninstaller silently so those are removed too.
Cache, downloads and settings live in %APPDATA%\Tencent\QQMusic, so nothing needs to be persisted.
The bundled updater (QQMusicUp.exe) can replace files inside the app directory; decline its update prompt and run 'scoop update qqmusic' instead.
